einzeiler: Songwriter Wyatt McCubbin talks about his debut album 650 and his musical journey.
kurzfassung: Songwriter Wyatt McCubbin joins the show to discuss his upcoming debut album, 650. He shares stories about growing up in a general store in Ohio, his time working on the radio with local legend Chubby Howard, and the personal experiences behind his music. The conversation also covers family life on tour and the importance of stepping away from the digital world.
stichpunkte: Wyatt McCubbin discusses his debut album 650, releasing on October 16
He grew up in a converted general store in Selma, Ohio, run by his family
He shares memories of working in radio alongside 85-year-old steel guitar legend Chubby Howard
The album's closing track marks the exact date he stopped drinking in December 2023
He talks about writing the emotional father-son song Boy in the Boat
He describes taking his young family on tour with him across the country
Producer Dave Cobb helped shape the album by asking family members for their favorite songs

clips.text: After getting pulled over for crossing double white lines, the driver realizes his license has been expired for quite a long time.

clips.hook: Growing up across the street from grandpa's shop
clips.text: The guest describes spending every afternoon after school tinkering with old cars and trucks in his grandfather's garage.
Working alongside an elderly co-host involved managing basic studio technology and listening to endless stories about classic country artists.

clips.hook: Deciding to put down the bottle for good
clips.text: Before taking a trip to Las Vegas, the artist decided it was time to take a permanent break from alcohol after drinking casually since youth.

clips.hook: Taking young kids on a tour bus
clips.text: Traveling across the country on a tour bus with toddlers brings unexpected joy and provides a much better experience than video calls.

beschreibung:
Wyatt McCubbin joins The Brothers Hunt, also known as Dan and Reid Isbell, on God’s Country for an episode packed with country music history, hilarious stories and an inside look at the life of a Nashville songwriter.Wyatt shares how he went from working in small-town country radio to writing songs recorded by artists like Zach Top, Luke Combs, Lainey Wilson and Jon Pardi.

He also opens up about his friendship with country music legend Marty Stuart, the story behind his Grand Ole Opry debut and what it was like helping create Zach Top’s breakout sound.The guys also get into Wyatt’s Ohio upbringing, his love for traditional country music, the realities of chasing songs in Nashville and plenty of stories that probably shouldn’t have made it onto the air.If you love classic country, songwriting stories, hunting, the outdoors and conversations that feel more like hanging around deer camp, this episode is for you.

Subscribe to The Brothers Hunt for new episodes of God’s Country every week, featuring country artists, hit songwriters and outdoorsmen sharing the stories you won’t hear anywhere else.
